### Fixed
- SIP/DSL semantics batch (six P1 correctness fixes):
  - A dialog at its per-dialog message cap that keeps receiving
    retransmissions now counts as active.
    - A dropped at-cap retransmission still advances `updated_at`.
    - So idle compaction no longer evicts a dialog under a retransmission
      flood.
  - SIPREC multipart bodies are split only on line-anchored `--boundary`
    delimiters, per [RFC 2046](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046.html).
    - A boundary string occurring mid-line inside part content (metadata XML,
      SDP) no longer corrupts part extraction.
  - Repeated T.38 re-INVITEs (session refresh) emit `T38Switch` once, at the
    genuine audio→T.38 transition.
    - They no longer emit it on every other exchange.
    - A real return to audio and back re-emits correctly.
  - STIR/SHAKEN PASSporTs retain every `dest.tn` entry.
    - They also retain the previously-unparsed `dest.uri` array
      ([RFC 8225 section 5.2.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8225.html#section-5.2.1)).
    - Before, they kept only the first TN.
  - Filter-DSL numeric equality (`==`/`!=`) uses a domain-grounded tolerance.
    - The tolerance is 5e-4, half the finest millisecond-derived step.
    - It replaces `f64::EPSILON`, which was effectively exact-match for values
      ≥ 2.
    - `duration == 5` now matches computed durations.
  - `src.port`/`dst.port` in the filter DSL read ports captured at dialog
    creation.
    - They used to read the first *stored* message.
    - That silently swapped to a response's reversed ports after idle
      compaction drained old messages.

## [0.5.30] - 2026-07-24

### Changed
- The standalone Prometheus `/metrics` server now has its own `metrics`
  feature (enabled by default).
  - It is no longer gated behind `api`.
  - It uses a raw TCP listener with no axum/tokio.
  - So `--metrics` now works in the default build, which does not enable
    `api`.
  - Previously it silently did nothing there.

### Fixed
- `sipnab_messages_total` now reports the same value from the REST `/metrics`
  endpoint and the standalone metrics server.
  - Both count SIP messages by method.
  - The REST endpoint previously counted one per dialog.
  - That undercounted every multi-message dialog.
- The synthetic packet builder (pcap export of SIP messages) truncates a SIP
  payload larger than a single IPv4 datagram can hold.
  - So the IP/UDP length fields match the bytes written.
  - Before, the fields saturated while the full oversized payload was
    appended.
  - That left header and content disagreeing.
- `GET /v1/streams/{ssrc}` now returns the most-active stream when several
  streams share an SSRC (endpoint collision).
  - It does so deterministically.
  - Before, an arbitrary match could let a colliding orphan shadow the real
    media stream.
- The event-exec engine now kills and reaps a child process whose status check
  errors.
  - It used to forget it.
  - The child could previously linger as a zombie.
- A 200 OK to INVITE that races a CANCEL now correctly establishes the call
  (Canceled → InCall), per RFC 3261.
  - Before, a call that was actually answered stayed stuck in the Canceled
    state.
- A 401/407 auth challenge to REGISTER no longer marks the registration
  Failed.
  - Challenges are intermediate. The client re-registers with credentials.
  - So the dialog stays auth-pending until a genuine failure or a 200 OK.
- Call answer time (`answered_at`) is now pinned to the initial INVITE's
  CSeq.
  - So a re-INVITE's 200 OK can no longer be recorded as the call's answer
    time.
  - That corrupted setup/ring metrics.
- `cseq()` returns only the single RFC 3261 method token.
  - It drops trailing garbage (`1 INVITE extra` → `INVITE`).
  - That garbage previously defeated method comparisons in timing.
- The From/To user is now extracted from the actual addressable URI.
  - That is inside the angle brackets of a name-addr, or the bare addr-spec.
  - It is never a quoted display name.
  - So a crafted `"sip:evil@x"` display name can no longer spoof the user.
  - A non-sip URI such as `tel:` yields no user.
- `--split filesize:N` now counts each record's on-disk framing, not just the
  payload.
  - The framing is the pcap record header, or the pcap-ng EPB overhead.
  - So rotation fires at the intended file size, instead of systematically
    overshooting it.
- HEP v3 packet building now truncates an oversized SIP payload to fit the
  protocol's 16-bit length fields.
  - Before, the total length could wrap into a corrupt header that a collector
    would misframe.
- The pcap-ng reader resets its timestamp resolution and link type to the
  defaults at each Section Header Block.
  - So a multi-section capture whose later section omits `if_tsresol` no
    longer inherits the previous section's resolution.
  - That misread packet timestamps.
- WAV export from the call list now saves the audio of the row the user has
  highlighted.
  - The selection is resolved against the displayed order (filter + search +
    sort).
  - It used to resolve against raw store order.
  - Under an active filter or sort, that exported a different dialog's audio.
- The "clear matching / clear non-matching" call-list actions now evaluate each
  dialog against its real RTP streams.
  - Previously they passed an empty stream slice to the filter.
  - So a dialog that matched only via a stream criterion was misclassified.
    - The criteria are `rtp.codec`/`rtp.mos`/`rtp.jitter`/`rtp.loss`.
  - In "clear non-matching", such a dialog was wrongly deleted.
- RTCP-reported jitter is now converted from RTP-timestamp units to
  milliseconds (`jitter * 1000 / clock_rate`).
  - That happens before it overwrites a stream's jitter estimate.
  - It used to be stored raw.
  - The old code fed MOS a jitter 8x too large for an 8 kHz stream.
- The RTCP cumulative-packets-lost field is now decoded as the 24-bit *signed*
  value RFC 3550 specifies (sign-extended into an `i32`).
  - A negative count (net duplicates) previously zero-extended into a huge
    positive loss total.
  - Stream loss counters clamp a negative value to zero.
- Interarrival jitter now interprets the RTP-timestamp difference as a signed
  (`i32`) transit delta.
  - So a reordered packet no longer produces a ~4.29e9-unit spike.
  - That spike corrupted the estimate.

## [0.5.29] - 2026-07-23

### Security
- The REST API now rate-limits **before** authenticating.
  - So a flood of wrong-token requests is throttled per-IP (503).
  - It no longer returns an unbounded stream of 401s.
  - That closes an unlimited-speed Bearer-token brute-force window.
- The SIP parser's per-line length cap now bounds a single *unfolded* header
  line, not only folded continuations.
  - A multi-megabyte header with no continuation lines is rejected
    (parse_error, header dropped).
  - It is no longer buffered whole.
- The HEP receiver's per-peer rate limiter fails closed when its tracking
  table is full.
  - A brand-new source IP is dropped, rather than bypassing the per-peer cap.
  - So a many-source-IP flood can no longer exhaust the table to win a free
    pass.
  - This does not affect already-tracked peers.
- TLS keylog entries now zeroize all key material on drop.
  - That covers the secret, the client random, and the label.
  - It goes through the `zeroize` crate, a non-elidable write.
  - It replaces a plain byte loop.
    - The compiler could optimize that loop away.
    - It never cleared the label.
- The generated `tshark` command now POSIX-quotes every interpolated value:
  - input file,
  - device,
  - BPF and display filters.
  - Embedded single quotes get proper `'\''` escaping.
  - So a crafted filename or filter can no longer break out of the quoting to
    inject shell words.
- The Mermaid call-flow export escapes untrusted SIP-derived labels.
  - Message and participant labels are neutralized for the Mermaid layer.
    - Newlines become spaces.
    - `#;<>` become Mermaid entity codes.
  - The standalone HTML export additionally HTML-escapes the whole diagram.
  - That closes an XSS: a crafted label could close the `<pre>` block and
    inject a live `<script>`.

### Fixed
- pcap loading in the TUI now routes packet timestamps through the shared,
  hardened `pcap_ts_to_chrono` converter.
  - It clamps `tv_usec` before the microsecond→nanosecond multiply.
  - The previous raw `(tv_usec as u32) * 1000` overflowed on a crafted or
    nanosecond-precision capture.
    - It panicked in debug.
    - It gave a wrong timestamp in release.
- Four UTF-8 byte-boundary panics reachable from real input.
  - All now go through a shared `text::floor_char_boundary` helper, or
    whole-character slicing:
    - `--payload-limit` truncation mid-character in CLI output.
    - The TUI filter-field renderer:
      - cursor on a multibyte character,
      - cursor past the visible field width,
      - unfocused truncation mid-character,
      - plus the filter dialog's byte-stepping cursor when typing/editing
        multibyte text.
    - The save/file-open path cursor cell.
      - The two duplicated span builders are now one.
    - `--alert` duration parsing with a multibyte suffix.
      - It now reads as an invalid suffix, instead of panicking.

## [0.5.28] - 2026-07-23

### Documentation
- Crate-wide documentation pass.
  - It covers every module, function (public, private, and test), type,
    field, and constant.
  - That spans `src/`, all integration test crates, and the fuzz targets.
  - Each now carries rustdoc describing:
    - purpose,
    - arguments,
    - returns,
    - errors,
    - and explicit side effects (I/O, locks, subprocess execution, privilege
      drops, raw-socket sends, detector/cache state).
  - `clippy::missing_docs_in_private_items` enforces it going forward.
  - That sits alongside the existing `missing_docs` gate.
  - CI clippy runs `-D warnings`.
  - Around twenty stale or misattached doc blocks were corrected to match the
    code.
  - ~250 code-improvement observations recorded during the audit are filed in
    `tasks/todo.md`.

### Added
- Capture: SIP over SCTP.
  - `parse_packet` now decodes the SCTP common header and chunk stream.
  - It extracts the SIP payload from the first complete (B+E) DATA chunk.
  - It recovers the real source/destination ports.
  - Any truncated or malformed SCTP input fails closed to an empty payload.
    - So downstream never misreads transport bytes as SIP.
  - Single unfragmented DATA chunk per packet.
  - Multi-packet fragment reassembly is a documented follow-up.
  - Enables SIGTRAN/Diameter (3GPP IMS) environments.
- TUI: packet-loss % trend row on the quality dashboard.
  - It sits alongside the existing MOS and jitter sparklines.
  - Good/warn/bad loss thresholds set its color.
  - A legend names all three metrics with units.
  - That completes the real-time MOS/jitter/loss view.
- TUI: call-timeline view (`T` from the call list).
  - It is a horizontal, proportional time axis of call phases.
    - setup → ringing → in-call → teardown,
    - or the failed/canceled path.
  - It is derived from dialog timing milestones.
  - It has:
    - per-phase duration labels,
    - phase colors,
    - a legend,
    - and a PDD/ring/setup/teardown summary line.
  - It degrades gracefully for never-answered calls and dialogs without timing
    data.

### Fixed
- Privilege drop: a nonexistent `--user` is now reported as "not found".
  - It comes with the `useradd`/`--user` guidance.
  - This applies on hosts whose NSS stack (e.g. sss/systemd modules) signals a
    missing user via an `ENOENT`/`ESRCH` return from `getpwnam_r`.
  - Before, it surfaced a raw "No such file or directory" OS error.
  - This does not affect plain-glibc hosts.

## [0.5.25] - 2026-07-22

### Performance
- TUI: the 0.5.24 churn-rebuild floor now covers every store-derived view, not
  just the call list.
  - Stream-list rows were re-filtered from the whole store on every frame and
    every keypress, under a blocking read.
  - They now derive once per tick into a keyed cache.
  - Keypresses navigate it lock-free.
  - These all refresh at the floor (~3/s) under data churn:
    - the quality-dashboard snapshot (rebuilt every tick while open),
    - the statistics aggregation (every dialog, every frame),

      worst in extended/multi-leg flows).

  - A completed background pcap load clears the floors.
  - So every view reflects the file on the very next tick.

## [0.5.18] - 2026-07-20

### Changed
- `-O` pcap output is written by a hand-rolled buffered writer, instead of
  libpcap's `Savefile` (WS8.3).
  - Classic pcap records go through a 512 KiB `BufWriter`.
  - They no longer take one FFI call + locked stdio `fwrite` per packet.
  - Per-packet write cost −43% (same-toolchain A/B).
  - +8–16% end-to-end single-core on x86.
  - End-to-end unchanged on the aarch64 reference host.
    - There, re-emit is bound by data volume rather than per-packet overhead.
  - This corrects the +8.3% first published for this entry.
    - That figure compared binaries of different build provenance.
  - Write errors (full disk, dead mount) now surface as errors.
  - libpcap used to discard them silently.

## [0.5.12] - 2026-07-17

### Added

- **Security**: scanner-kill responses (`-K`/`--kill-target`,
  `--kill-scanner`) can now **source-spoof** the victim's `ip:port` via a raw
  socket.
  - So the reply appears to come from the SIP listener the scanner targeted.
  - It no longer comes from sipnab's ephemeral port.
  - `--kill-spoof {auto|raw|ephemeral}` controls it (default `auto`):
    - `auto` spoofs when `CAP_NET_RAW` is available (already granted for live
      capture). Otherwise it falls back to the ephemeral source.
    - `raw` requires spoofing. It errors if the raw socket cannot be opened.
    - `ephemeral` never spoofs.
  - Linux-only. Other platforms always use the ephemeral source.
  - New metric
    `sipnab_kill_responses_sent_total{mode="raw"|"ephemeral"}`
    exposes which path was used.

## [0.5.11] - 2026-07-17

### Fixed

- **Security**: `-K` / `--kill-target` and `--kill-scanner` now actually
  transmit the SIP kill response to the scanner over UDP.
  - The worker previously did three things:
    - matched the target,
    - built the response,
    - and rate-limited it.
  - But it only logged `Scanner-kill: would send <N> byte response to <address>:<port>`, without putting anything on the wire.
    - pcap injection was a stub.
  - Send failures now surface as an error, instead of silently vanishing.
  - The response leaves from an ephemeral source port.
  - It does not leave from the SIP listener port the scanner targeted.
    - Source-port matching would need raw sockets / `CAP_NET_RAW`.
    - That is tracked as future work.

## [0.5.10] - 2026-07-17

### Added

- **Display**: `--proto-number` — annotate the transport tag with the IANA IP
  protocol number (`UDP(17)`, `TCP(6)`).
  - TLS and WS report their TCP carrier's number.
  - The number identifies the IP-layer transport, not the SIP framing.
- **Capture**: `-x` / `--quiet-bad-parse` — suppress the per-packet SIP
  parse-error diagnostic for SIP-looking-but-unparseable packets.
  - The packet is dropped either way.
  - Only the notice is silenced.

## [0.5.9] - 2026-07-16

### Added

- **TUI**: the F10 column selector now saves the current column layout with
  `s`.
  - It writes `[display] visible_columns` into your sipnabrc.
  - So it persists across runs.
  - Previously the layout had to be hand-edited into the config.
- **Capture**: `-S` / `--limitlen <BYTES>` — parse only the first N bytes of
  each packet.
  - This is independent of the capture snaplen and the display truncation.
- **Capture**: `--no-reassembly` — disable IP-fragment and TCP-segment
  reassembly.
  - It is the inverse of segment reassembly.
  - sipnab parses every packet standalone.

## [0.5.8] - 2026-07-16

### Added

- **Capture**: `-p` / `--no-promisc` — do not put the interface into
  promiscuous mode.
  - Promiscuous mode stays on by default for a named device.
  - It is never on for the `any` pseudo-device.
  - Also settable via `[capture] promisc`.
- **SIP**: `[sip] xcid_headers` — configurable B2BUA leg-correlation header
  names (`sip.xcid`).
  - Defaults to `["X-Call-ID"]`.
  - Add carrier-specific headers (e.g. `["X-Call-ID", "X-CID"]`), so
    multi-leg calls correlate.
- **HEP**: two new options for `--hep-send`:
  - `--hep-auth <KEY>`: the Homer authenticate-key `0x000e` chunk. It is also
    read from `SIPNAB_HEP_AUTH`.
  - `--hep-id <ID>`: the capture-agent id `0x000c` chunk, default 1.
  - Previously the sender emitted no auth key, and a hardcoded capture id of 1.

## [0.5.7] - 2026-07-16

### Added

- **Security**: `-K` / `--kill-target <ADDR[:PORT-RANGE]>` — targeted scanner
  kill.
  - It sends the kill response to any SIP request whose source matches the
    given address and an optional port range.
    - Examples: `192.0.2.1:5060-5090`, `[::1]:5060`.
  - It does so regardless of UA/behavioral detection.
  - Repeatable.
  - It spawns the kill worker on its own. So `--kill-scanner` is not required.
  - Malformed targets are rejected at startup.

## [0.5.6] - 2026-07-16

### Added

- **Matching**: new `-e` / `--match <PATTERN>` flag — the the terminal SIP
  tools payload match-expression.
  - A regex is tested against the whole raw SIP message.
  - Once any message in a dialog matches, every later message of that dialog
    is emitted too (dialog-following).
  - It honors `-i`/`-v`/`-w`/
    `--single-line`.
  - It is independent of the trailing BPF filter positional.

### Fixed

- **CLI**: corrected a misleading `--help` example.
  - It presented `'INVITE sip:'` as a BPF filter.
  - That is not valid BPF.
  - The examples now show a real BPF filter and the new `-e` payload grep.

## [0.5.5] - 2026-07-13

### Added

- **TUI**: `w` toggles line wrapping in the call-flow detail panel.
  - With wrapping off:
    - long header lines truncate,
    - ←/→ scroll the focused panel horizontally,
    - and a horizontal scrollbar tracks the widest line along the panel's
      bottom edge.
  - `End` in the focused panel now jumps to the bottom of the message.
  - `Home` also rewinds the horizontal scroll.

### Fixed

- **TUI**: the call-flow detail panel's scrollbar and scroll range are now
  computed from the *wrapped* rows that actually render.
  - Some messages had long headers that wrapped past the pane height, while
    their logical line count fit.
  - They showed no scrollbar, and ignored Up/Down.
  - Line wrapping also switched from word-wrap to full-width character wrap.
  - So row accounting is exact.

## [0.5.4] - 2026-07-13

### Added

- **Packaging**: releases now include `.rpm` packages (RHEL/Fedora) for
  `x86_64` and `aarch64`.
  - Each comes in standard and `-noaudio` variants.
  - That mirrors the `.deb` set (`contrib/rpm/build-rpm.sh`).
  - The v0.5.3 release was backfilled with RPMs built from the released
    binaries.

### Fixed

- **TUI**: the screen no longer flashes blank every few seconds on busy live
  captures, even when the displayed page isn't changing.
  - A render tick could lose the store-lock race to the processing thread.
  - It then flushed a frame with an empty main pane.
  - The next frame repainted it.
  - A tick now does one of two things:
    - draws from a consistent snapshot of both stores,
    - or skips the frame entirely, leaving the previous frame on screen.
  - Sustained contention forces a blocking frame after a few skipped ticks.
  - So a write-saturated capture degrades to a briefly stale frame, instead of
    a flickering or frozen UI.
  - Deferred save and audio-decode work now only runs after its status frame
    ("Saving capture.pcap…" or "Decoding audio…") actually painted.

## [0.5.3] - 2026-07-09

### Added

- **TUI**: pcap files now load on a background worker, with a live status
  line such as "Loading capture.pcap… 50000 packets".
  - Opening a large capture no longer freezes the interface.
  - Dialogs appear progressively while the file parses.
  - Saves and audio decode likewise defer behind a visible
    "Saving capture.pcap…" or "Decoding audio…" status.
  - The Mermaid clipboard copy runs detached, with a bounded wait.
    - So a wedged xclip can't hang the UI.
- **TUI**:
  - `n`/`N` jump to the next/previous search match in the raw-message view
    (wrapping, vim/less style).

- **TUI**:
  - `NO_COLOR` is honored.
    - The theme collapses to terminal defaults.
    - That includes the previously hardcoded RGB status-bar background.
  - Terminals below 40x6 get an explicit too-small notice, instead of a
    garbled screen.
  - The live-capture empty state says it is waiting for traffic, instead of
    speculating about pcap files.
- **TUI**: some rebinds now warn at startup:
  - rebinding a key that a view already uses as a built-in,
  - or binding two actions to the same key.
  - Such rebinds silently never fired.
- **CLI**:
  - `--completions <shell>` generates bash/zsh/fish/elvish/

  - `--help` groups its flags under section headings, instead of one flat

- **CLI**:
  - An unknown `--filter` field now names the field, suggests the closest
    valid one, and lists the valid set.
  - A typo'd `-d <device>` lists the available interfaces.
  - The docs list the exit codes (0/1/2).


### Fixed

- `--mcp` in a build without the `mcp` feature silently ran a plain batch
  capture with no server.
  - It now fails fast with exit 2, like every other feature-gated flag.
  - `--hep-listen` gates early too.
- Some API startup failures failed silently
, on a detached thread behind
  the TUI:
  - a busy `--api` port,
  - an unauthenticated non-loopback bind,
  - or TLS flags.
  - The listener is now bound before the TUI starts.
  - The error is fatal and visible.
  - Bad `--mcp-bind`/`--mcp-transport` values are fatal, instead of
    log-and-skip.
- The MCP `tail_dialogs` tool's `source_exhausted` field was a hardcoded
  `false` stub.
  - It now flips to `true` when a pcap replay is fully consumed.
  - So polling clients can stop.
- `--json-pretty` produced byte-identical output to `--json`.
  - It now pretty-prints each message.
  - It is still a parseable JSON stream.
- `--call-report` with an unknown Call-ID warned on stderr, but exited 0.
  - It now exits 1.
- An explicit `--portrange 5060-5061` lost to a config-file range.
  - clap couldn't distinguish it from the default.
- A filter expression could panic while rendering the parse error.
  - The trigger was exotic whitespace before a multibyte character at the
    error position.
  - The `filter_dsl_parse_is_total` property test found it.
  - Parsing is total again.
- The man page declared the wrong license and a stale version.
  - It said GPL-3.0-only instead of MIT OR Apache-2.0.
  - Both are fixed.
  - Drift tests plus a pre-commit gate covering docs version strings now guard
    them.
- **TUI**:
  - The F7 filter and `N` name dialogs closed and discarded the typed input on
    a validation error.
  - They now stay open, with the error shown inline.
  - The help overlay's stale `u` (From/To modes) and F2 (save formats)
    descriptions were corrected.
  - They are drift-tested.

### Changed

- **TUI**: in the F7 filter dialog, the **All** master checkbox moved above
  the method grid (above REGISTER).
  - Tab/arrow traversal follows the new order: text fields → All → methods →
    buttons.

    Home/End move the highlight in the live-narrowed call and stream lists.

## [0.5.0] - 2026-07-06

> The v0.5.0 release assets were rebuilt on 2026-07-08 from the re-pointed
> tag.
> They additionally contain the fixes below, plus the new `-noaudio.deb`
> variants.
> Checksums differ from the 2026-07-06 build.
>
> - TUI: call/stream-list selection clamped on display-list shrink.
>   - It was a slice-out-of-range panic when a narrowed list got shorter.
> - TUI: Enter with two or more starred rows opens one chronologically merged
>   flow of all of them ().
>   - It has per-row dialog attribution in detail/raw/naming.
> - TUI: a persisted search query that narrows the list is shown on the status
>   line (`Search: /q`).
>   - F9 clears it, with the filter.
> - New `[crash]` config section.
>   - A panic hook restores the terminal.
>   - It writes a crash report with a full backtrace.
>   - It has an optional core-dump mode.
> - Filter popup gained an "All" master checkbox for the method grid.
> - pcapng writer now declares `if_tsresol=9`.
>   - Files previously read with all times inflated ×1000 ("year 58484").
>   - A repair script for old captures ships as
>     `scripts/repair_pcapng_tsresol.py`.
> - Call list gained a sortable Duration column alongside PDD.

### Added — activated the dormant fuzzing & property-test safety nets (WS7)

- The 11 compile-only libFuzzer targets now actually run on a schedule.
- Four new targets cover untrusted-input surfaces that had none.
- Three proptest properties assert semantic invariants the fuzzers can't:

- **Weekly `Fuzz` workflow** (`.github/workflows/fuzz.yml`):
  - A 15-target matrix runs each libFuzzer target on nightly.
    - The default is 300s, configurable via `workflow_dispatch`.
  - It is primed from the tracked seed corpora.
  - It uploads any crash/timeout reproducer as an artifact.
  - CI's existing `fuzz-check` still compile-checks the targets on every push.
- **New fuzz targets** for the untrusted-input surfaces that lacked one:
  - the pure-Rust pcap/pcapng reader (`sipnab -I hostile.pcapng`),
  - the DTLS-SRTP handshake observer,
  - TCP stream reassembly (structured segment interleavings),
  - and the hand-rolled SIPREC XML scanner.
- **Property tests** (`tests/property_test.rs`, proptest):
  - SIP build→parse field round-trip,
  - SDP build→parse→rebuild stability,
  - and the filter DSL as a total function on arbitrary text (parse + evaluate
    never panic).

### Changed — **BREAKING (library API, 0.5.0)**: typed errors for the crate-root parse/capture surface (WS6.1)

- The functions and types re-exported at the crate root no longer return
  `anyhow::Result`.
- They return structured, matchable error enums.
  - These are `sipnab::ParseError` / `sipnab::CaptureError`.
  - Both are `#[non_exhaustive]`.

- `parse_sip` / `parse_sip_bytes` / `parse_rtp_header` / `parse_sdp`
  → `Result<_, ParseError>`.
  - Example variants:
    - `TooShort { what, need, got }`,
    - `BadRtpVersion { version }`,
    - `NotSip { line }`,
    - `BadSdpVersion { version }`.
- `parse_packet` / `PcapReader::new` → `Result<_, CaptureError>`.
  - Example variants:
    - `UnsupportedLinkType(i32)`,
    - `EncapTooDeep { kind, limit }`,
    - `NetMonFormat`,
    - `UnknownFormat { magic }`.

- Some callers propagated these errors into `anyhow::Result`, or only
  `Display`ed them.
  - They keep working unchanged.
  - Both enums implement `std::error::Error`.
- Callers that matched on message text must switch to matching variants.
  - That is the point of the change.

- Additionally **BREAKING**: `Error::ConfigRead` / `Error::ConfigParse` now
  carry the underlying `std::io::Error` / `toml::de::Error` as a real
  `#[source]`.
  - The field is renamed `reason: String` → `source`.
  - So the error chain is inspectable via `source()`.

### Changed — **BREAKING (library API, 0.5.0)**: API-guidelines sweep (WS6.2)

- Sixteen growth-prone public enums are now `#[non_exhaustive]`.
- So adding a variant stops being a semver-major event.
  - Examples: a new fraud pattern, RTCP packet type, cipher suite or
    transport.
- The enums:
  - `FraudType`,
  - `DigestVulnerability`,
  - `RtcpPacket`,
  - `XrBlock`,
  - `TransportProto`,
  - `SdpEvent`,
  - `OfferAnswer`,
  - `CorrelationReason`,
  - `Attestation`,
  - `VerificationStatus`,
  - `HepProtocol`,
  - `CipherSuite`,
  - `SrtpProfile`,
  - `TlsContentType`,
  - `TlsVersion`,
  - `SrtpSuite`.
- Downstream `match`es on these enums now need a wildcard arm.
- Closed RFC sets (e.g. `SdpDirection`, `G711Codec`) deliberately stay
  exhaustively matchable.

- Non-breaking in the same sweep:
  - `DialogStore` and `StreamStore` now implement `Debug`.
  - The crate root documents the semver status of `#[doc(hidden)]` modules
    (no guarantee).
  - The `SipMessage::to_*` accessors and the `as_str` receiver difference are
    documented in place, as deliberate naming decisions.
  - The wasm `get_*` exports also stay as they are.
    - They are a JavaScript-facing API consumed by the website's analyzer
      page.
    - There, `get`-prefixed accessors are idiomatic.
    - The exported names are the stable JS contract.

### Added — compiled doctests for the top library entry points (WS6.3)

- Every major entry point now carries a compiled, asserted example:
  - `parse_sip`,
  - `parse_rtp_header`,
  - `parse_sdp`,
  - `parse_packet`,
  - `PcapReader` (in-memory and `no_run` file variants),
  - `FilterExpr` (previously an `ignore`d fence),
  - `DialogStore`,
  - `StreamStore`,
  - `estimate_mos`,
  - `SipMethod::as_str`,
  - and matchable-error examples on `ParseError` / `CaptureError`.
- 17 doctests run in CI.
  - Up from 4 compiled + 1 ignored.
- Compiled examples are the only ones CI keeps honest.
## [0.4.19] - 2026-07-03

### Fixed — multi-stream (audio + video) SDP timeline

- Some calls offer more than one media stream (e.g. `m=audio` **and**
  `m=video`).
- They had the video leg dropped from the per-dialog SDP timeline / `--json`
  output.
- `extract_media_info` recorded only the first `m=` line.
- The timeline now aggregates codecs across **all** media descriptions.
  - It keeps `m=` order, de-duplicated.
  - So a video call lists both PCMU and H264/VP8.
- (RTP stream *linking* already tracked every media stream correctly.
  - Both audio and video streams associate to the dialog and resolve their
    codecs.
  - This only fixes the timeline/report view.)

### Added — all 19 IANA-registered compact header forms

- sipnab previously expanded only the ten RFC 3261 core compact header names
  (`c e f i k l m s t v`).
- The nine IANA-registered extension forms now expand too:
  - `a` Accept-Contact,
  - `b` Referred-By,
  - `d` Request-Disposition,
  - `j` Reject-Contact,
  - `o` Event,
  - `r` Refer-To,
  - `u` Allow-Events,
  - `x`
    Session-Expires,
  - `y` Identity.
- Two of these fixed real analysis gaps:

- **STIR/SHAKEN evasion fixed:**
  - Consider an INVITE carrying its PASSporT in the compact `y:` form
    (RFC 8224).
  - It was invisible to `--stir-shaken` analysis.
  - It remained fully valid to real verifiers.
  - Compact-form Identity headers are now extracted identically to the long
    form.
  - Regression test: `compact_identity_header_cannot_evade_extraction`.
- **Transfer tracking:**
  - A REFER using `r:` ([RFC 3515](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3515.html)) now drives the `Transferring`
    dialog state and `refer_to`, like the long form.

- Determination and design are in docs/design/compact-headers-spec.md.
- SigComp ([RFC 3320](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3320.html) "compressed SIP") remains explicitly out of scope.

### Changed — one canonical dialog/stream summary across all surfaces (WS3)

- "Dialog summary" was implemented five times:
  - CLI/NDJSON,
  - REST API,
  - MCP,
  - TUI save,
  - reports.
- The copies had drifted on the wire.
- All surfaces now project through
  `output::model::{DialogSummary, StreamSummary}`.
- A consistency test pins the shared shape.
- **Wire changes:**

- **MCP** `list_dialogs`/`tail_dialogs`/`find_problems`:
  - `message_count` → `msg_count`.
  - `method` is now the canonical SIP form (`INVITE`).
    - It was previously the Debug form `Invite`.
  - Rows gain `duration_sec` and `timing`.
- **REST API** `/v1/dialogs`: `from`/`to` → `from_user`/`to_user`.
  - The values always were the URI user parts.
- **TUI JSON save**:
  - `message_count` → `msg_count`.
  - `created_at` gains full RFC 3339 precision.
  - Rows gain `updated_at`/`duration_sec`.
- RTP JSON save:
  - `mos`/`jitter_ms`/`loss_pct` are no longer rounded to 1 decimal.
  - MOS now comes from the single E-model in `rtp::quality`.
    - This path carried its own divergent copy.
  - An unset codec serializes as `null`, instead of `"unknown"`.
- The browser/WASM `get_dialogs` surface intentionally keeps its current
  shape.
  - Website JS consumes it.
  - docs/design/maintainability-perf-spec.md tracks unifying it.

## [0.4.18] - 2026-07-02

### Fixed — TUI correctness sweep

**Message visibility (critical):**
- **OPTIONS/REGISTER keepalives are no longer misclassified as
  retransmissions.**
  - Retransmission identity now includes the top Via branch.
    - That is the RFC 3261 transaction ID.
  - So distinct transactions that reuse Call-ID + CSeq all render in the
    ladder.
    - That is the common keepalive pattern.
  - Messages without a branch (RFC 2543 peers) keep the CSeq-identity
    fallback.
- **Folding is identical in every timestamp mode.**
  - Fold decisions were keyed on list positions.
  - `Scaled` mode's spacer rows shifted those positions.
  - So which messages were visible depended on the time-unit setting.
  - Every ladder row now carries the index of the raw message it renders.
  - Folds, expansion and selection are keyed on that.
- **Fold headers show their count on the arrow** (`OPTIONS (+2 retx)`).
  - The off-arrow annotation was hidden under the split detail pane.
  - That made folds read as silent data loss.
  - The ladder pane clips annotations.
- **`e` expands the fold you have selected**, and re-collapses it.
  - It is header-keyed.
  - It reveals all retransmissions of the run.

**Selection & filters:**
- **Enter opens the row the user sees.**
  - These all resolve against the same displayed list the renderer draws
    (filter + search + sort):
    - selection,
    - navigation bounds,
    - counts,
    - and endpoint lookups.
  - Sorting or searching no longer opens the wrong call.
- **Reversing the sort on the default `#` column works**
  - It was a no-op.
- **Multi-select checkmarks are keyed by Call-ID**
  - So re-sorting, filtering or new traffic can no longer silently transfer a
    checkmark to a different call before save/clear acts on it.
- **Filter fields match literally.**
  - User text is regex-escaped.
  - `a+b` means the user `a+b`.
  - `(`/quotes/backslashes can no longer break the filter.
- **The Payload filter field works**
  - A new `payload` DSL field matches the raw message content of a dialog.
- **The stream list honors search and the active SIP display filter**
  - It does so via each stream's associated dialog.
  - Unassociated streams stay visible.
- Smaller fixes:
  - Search reopen keeps the query for refining.
  - The call-flow detail pane shows the selected message, even with folds or a
    transaction filter active.
  - Per-call state (marks, folds, diff selection) resets when opening a
    different call.
  - Esc from a raw message returns to the view it was opened from.

**Navigation:**
- **Scroll offsets are clamped to content everywhere**
  - That covers: raw message, combined detail, stream detail, call-flow
    ladder, statistics, diff.
  - `End` lands on the last page, instead of a blank screen.
  - Over-scrolling no longer strands `Up` presses.
- **The Statistics and Message-diff views scroll** (arrows, PgUp/PgDn,
  Home/End).
  - Long content was previously truncated, with no way to see it.
- Missing keys added:
  - `End` (raw message, stream detail),
  - `PgUp`/`PgDn` (stream list).
- The call-flow ladder keeps the selection inside the real viewport.
  - No more hardcoded 20-row guess.
- **Mouse wheel scrolls every view.**
- Key bursts/pastes are drained per frame, instead of one event per redraw.

**Keymap & settings:**
- Custom keybindings apply in the diff and combined-detail views.
  - quit/help were hardcoded there.
- A key rebound in the keymap wins over the built-in global `v`/`n`
  fallbacks.
- **Autoscroll works**
  - With the toggle on and the selection at the bottom, new calls pull the
    selection down (sticky-bottom).
  - A selection elsewhere is never yanked.
- **The syntax-highlight toggle works**
  - `s` in the raw view now actually renders plain text when off.
- `←`/`→` in the call flow explain themselves when the split pane is off.
  - They used to do nothing.
- The dead `call_flow_cache` is gone.

## [0.4.17] - 2026-06-24

### Call flow
- **RTP-in-flow is shown in every media segment, not just the first.**
  - A bar is now drawn after each INVITE transaction that carries media:
    - the initial call,
    - *and* each re-INVITE that re-establishes the stream.
  - It is keyed on the INVITE CSeq.
    - So a single transaction (early media + its confirming ACK) still draws
      only one.
  - Previously a same-codec re-INVITE drew nothing.
  - That made the ladder look like media stopped before the re-INVITE.
  - It actually flowed through to the BYE.
  - A re-INVITE that switches codecs still shows the new codec.
- **Dropped the redundant "active" from the bar label**
  - It now reads `RTP · PCMU`.
  - The codec on the in-flow channel already conveys "active".
- Homepage hero regenerated.
  - The call now shows RTP flowing in both segments (before and after the
    re-INVITE).
  - The label is `RTP · PCMA`.

## [0.4.16] - 2026-06-24

### Call flow
- **RTP-in-flow rendered as a centered double-rail channel.**
  - The media bar in the call-flow ladder now draws as a centered `═` double
    rail.
  - It spans the gap between the two endpoint pipes
    (`render::rtp_channel_bar`).
  - It is a sustained media channel, visually distinct from the single-line
    `─` SIP arrows.
  - It fixes the old byte-width centering.
    - That left a wide label aligned off to the left.
- **The bar shows the codec actually USED, not the SDP offer list.**
  - An INVITE may offer several codecs while the call lands on one.
  - The bar now shows that single codec.
  - Its source is the observed RTP stream's payload type (authoritative).
  - It falls back to the negotiated SDP answer codec, for SIP-only captures.
  - A re-INVITE that switches codecs (PCMU → G722) draws a fresh bar.
    - The new bar shows the new codec for the second media segment.
- **Early-media placement.**
  - A provisional (1xx) response carrying SDP opens the channel at that point
    (ringback/IVR).
  - It no longer waits until after the ACK.

### Performance
- **Batched reader→worker hand-off removes the `--cores` regression.**
  - Focused research isolated the cause of the throughput collapse past
    `--cores 2`:
    - It was *not* the RTP/dialog reconstruction. Idle workers regressed
      identically.
    - It was *not* CPU starvation. There were 14 idle cores.
    - It was the **per-packet channel hop**.
  - Every send bounced a cache line across cores.
  - That coherency traffic scaled with worker count.
  - The reader now batches ~128 packets per shard into one channel send.
    - Channel depth is measured in batches.
    - So the in-flight packet cap stays the same.
  - That amortizes the cross-core hop ~128×.
  - Setup: the aarch64 runner (Jetson Thor, 14 cores), 535k-packet carrier
    corpus, median-of-5.
  - The cliff is gone.
  - Throughput holds **flat at ~2.2–2.5M pkts/s from cores 2 through 8**.
  - Before, it collapsed 1.9M → 842k → 500k:

  | cores | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | 2 | 1.91M | **2.51M** |
  | 4 | 0.84M | **2.26M** |
  | 8 | 0.50M | **2.16M** |

  - `--cores 4/8` were previously *slower* than single-threaded.
  - They are now the fastest.
  - The remaining flatness past cores 2 is the raw ceiling of the single
    sequential pcap reader.
    - That is read + buffer copy + host-pair peek.
    - It is the expected serial stage.
  - We measured CPU pinning and ruled it out as a fix.
    - +3–5% at cores 2/4, within noise.
    - ~0% at cores 8.
  - Affinity cannot eliminate coherency traffic on a single-cluster SoC with
    per-core-private L1d/L2.

## [0.4.15] - 2026-06-24

### Performance
- **SIMD CRLF scanning in the SIP parser** (`memchr`).
  - `find_crlf` is called per header line.
  - It replaced its scalar `windows(2).position()` with SIMD `memchr`.
  - The semantics are byte-identical.
  - A parity test validates that over the adversarial edge cases:
    - bare `\r`,
    - trailing `\r`,
    - embedded NUL,
    - empty.
- **Fused offline multi-core front-end.**
  - `--cores N` now reads the pcap directly and shards in one thread
    (`run_offline_parallel_file` + `peek_host_pair`).
  - That eliminates:
    - the separate capture-reader thread,
    - and the semaphore-capped channel between read and shard.
  - This lifts the `--cores 2` peak.
    - Carrier 40k corpus, aarch64: ~1.81M pkts/s.
    - That is **2.4× the terminal viewer**, while fully reconstructing calls +
      RTP streams.
  - `--cores 2` is the sweet spot.
  - Past 2–3, the ceiling is the single sequential pcap reader (and SoC memory
    bandwidth), not CPU count.

### Added
- **`Ctrl+R` toggles RTP-in-flow** in the TUI.
  - It is an alias for `F6`.
  - It is for terminals/
    recorders that can't send function keys.

### Changed
- Homepage hero now shows **real bidirectional RTP media** flowing in the
  call-flow ladder.
  - REGISTER → INVITE → RTP → re-INVITE → RTP → BYE.
  - Regenerated from a real PII-free capture.

## [0.4.14] - 2026-06-24

### Changed
- **`--jobs N` renamed to `--cores N`**
  - That is clearer for a capture analyzer.
  - `--jobs` was build-tool jargon.
  - Same semantics: offline reconstruction worker count.

### Added / Performance
- **Parse parallelization.**
  - The multi-core engine now shards *raw* packets.
    - It uses a cheap link+IP-header host-pair peek,
      `capture::parse::peek_host_pair`.
  - So each worker does its own parse + reassembly.
  - A single dispatcher no longer parses serially.
  - A flow's packets share a host pair, and route to one worker.
  - That keeps reassembly correct.
- **mimalloc** is now the native binary's global allocator.
  - Offline ingestion does one heap allocation per packet.
  - So the allocator was on the hot path.
    - It was ~7.5% of instructions in a callgrind profile.
  - This was the single biggest win.
- **`ahash`** replaces SipHash for the per-packet stores (`StreamStore`,
  `DialogStore` maps/indexes).
  - SipHash was ~7% of instructions.
  - ahash is far faster.
  - It stays DoS-resistant (random-seeded) for attacker-controlled keys.
- **`profiling` build profile** (`cargo build --profile profiling`)
  - Release codegen, with full symbols for perf/valgrind.

  - Combined result (40k-call carrier corpus, aarch64):
    - **`sipnab --cores 2` runs at ~1.57M pkts/s — 1.87× faster than the
      terminal viewer** (840k).
    - It does that while reconstructing all calls and full RTP-stream stats.
    - The terminal viewer does not do that.
  - The sweet spot is 2–3 cores.
  - Higher core counts regress.
    - The single dispatcher + store merge is the next bottleneck.

## [0.4.13] - 2026-06-24

### Added
- **Multi-core offline reconstruction (`--jobs N`).**
  - It applies to an offline pcap (`-I`) with `N>1`.
  - A dispatcher runs the serial L2/L3/L4 parse + reassembly.
  - It shards each packet by **host pair** to `N` worker threads.
    - Host pair is direction-independent.
    - So a flow and its bidirectional RTP stay on one worker.
  - The workers have thread-local dialog + stream stores.
  - At EOF the stores merge, with a global stream↔dialog reassociation.
  - That reproduces the single-threaded result, even when a call's SDP and its
    RTP were sharded to different workers.
  - Default `--jobs 1` stays the same.
  - It covers dialog + RTP-stream reconstruction, and `--report`/`--json`.
  - Advanced features stay single-threaded:
    - live capture,
    - per-message output ordering,
    - security detectors,
    - SRTP.
  - Measured 2.14× on a 40k-call carrier corpus.
  - Parity validated at jobs 1/2/4/8/12.

### Fixed
- **Per-RTP-packet quality-event overhead.**
  - For every RTP packet, the hot path did two things:
    - rebuilt a `StreamKey`,
    - and did a second stream-store lookup.
  - It did that only to call `fire_quality_event`.
  - That call no-ops when `--on-quality` is unset.
  - It is now guarded on `EventExecEngine::quality_events_enabled()`.
  - +21% throughput on the 20k-call carrier corpus (5.15s → 4.07s).

## [0.4.12] - 2026-06-24

### Fixed
- **O(n²) carrier-scale throughput collapse eliminated** (SNB-0015).
  - Processing a pcap with many concurrent calls collapsed super-linearly.
    - At 20k→30k→40k calls, throughput fell 340k→116k→47k pkts/s.
    - Load went ×1.6. Wall-time went ×10.
    - Cores were idle, and RSS was <1 GiB.
    - So it was algorithmic, not resource-bound.
  - There were two independent O(n²) sources in `StreamStore`.
  - Both were keyed on the active-stream count:
    - `link_endpoint`/`link_to_dialog` scanned the **entire** stream table.
      - They did it on every SDP-bearing SIP message, to find the streams on a
        media endpoint.
      - That is O(streams) per message, O(calls²) overall.
      - They now use an `endpoint_index`
        (`HashMap<(IpAddr,u16), Vec<StreamKey>>`).
      - It is maintained on insert/evict/clear, like the existing `ssrc_index`.
      - So linking is O(matching streams).
    - `ensure_capacity` evicted one stream at a time with
      `shift_remove_index(0)`.
      - That is O(n) on an `IndexMap`.
      - Past `--max-streams`, every new stream paid an O(streams) shift.
        - The default is 50000, reached at ~25k calls.
      - That is O(calls²). It was the **dominant** term.
      - It is the same bug `DialogStore` already fixed.
      - It now evicts in batches (10%) via `drain`.
      - That amortizes the shift to ~O(1) per insertion.

  - Result (14-core host, carrier SIP+RTP corpus ~93% RTP, offline):
    - 30k calls 27.68s→8.19s (3.4×),
    - 40k calls 90.95s→17.02s (5.3×),
    - 40k throughput 47k→251k pkts/s.
  - All calls are still reconstructed.

### Added
- **`SIPNAB_PERF_STATS=1` batch probe.**
  - It emits `endpoint_link_scan_visits` and `evict_shift_work` at the end of a
    batch run.
  - That is the per-run work that was quadratic.
  - So the scaling is observable, and a regression is caught early.
  - A performance-contract unit test guards each.

## [0.4.11] - 2026-06-24

### Added
- **`--alert-json` structured alert channel.**
  - Security alerts could previously only be consumed by scraping the human
    `[ALERT] <type> src=<ip> <detail>` stderr line.
  - That is brittle to any format change.
  - With `--alert-json`, each fired alert is also emitted as one JSON object
    per line on **stderr**: `{"ts","alert","src","detail"}`.
  - That is a stable machine channel.
  - stdout stays reserved for `--json` message output and the stdio MCP wire.
  - So the JSON alert lines go to stderr. That is safe even mid-MCP-session.
  - `serde_json` escapes attacker-controlled detail.
  - So a crafted UA/Call-ID can't break the line, or inject a field.

## [0.4.10] - 2026-06-23

### Fixed
- **IPv6-fragmented SIP is now reassembled and decoded** (SNB-0014).
  - The IPv4-fragment fix (SNB-0011, 0.4.9) handled IPv4 only.
  - IPv6 carries fragmentation in a **Fragment extension header**, not the base
    header.
  - But `parse_packet` hardcoded `ip_id`/`fragment_offset`/`more_fragments` to
    `None/None/false` for IPv6.
  - So `PacketProcessor` never routed IPv6 fragments to the reassembler.
  - Each fragment was mis-parsed as a whole datagram.
  - That silently dropped the message.
    - A large INVITE with SDP over IPv6 decoded to 0.
    - tshark saw it.
  - `parse_packet` now walks the IPv6 extension headers.
  - On a Fragment header, it pulls its offset / MF / 32-bit identification.
  - So the reassembler keys and reassembles it.
  - `reparse_transport` then recovers the transport header from the
    reassembled payload.
  - `ParsedPacket.ip_id` widened `u16 → u32`.
    - The IPv6 fragment id is 32-bit.
    - The IPv4 16-bit id casts up.

## [0.4.9] - 2026-06-23

Hardening release, driven by an adversarial review of the `siptest` harness.

- New fixtures and a field-level cross-check surfaced five real defects.
- Each was fixed tests-first (red → green), with adversarial-input coverage.

### Added
- **`--json` now emits `contact` and the raw `sdp` body** (SNB-0009).
  - `contact` carries the `Contact` header.
  - `sdp` is the raw body.
    - It is emitted only for `Content-Type: application/sdp` with a
      valid-UTF-8 body.
  - That lets consumers cross-check:
    - the routing target,
    - and the negotiated media (connection / `m=` / `a=rtpmap`) that
      dynamic-PT decode relies on.
  - `schema_version` stays 1 (optional fields).
  - This release updates the schema and `docs/output-formats.md`.
- **Extension-enumeration detection** (SNB-0010).
  - The scanner detector now tracks the set of distinct target extensions
    probed by a single source within the window.
    - The extension is the To user, falling back to R-URI.
  - It raises `detection=enumeration` when that set exceeds a threshold.
  - That catches a **UA-randomized, INVITE-based, or low-and-slow** sweep.
  - Signature (`ua_pattern`) and pure-rate detection both miss such a sweep.
  - INVITE now also counts toward the rate signal.
  - Bounded per source.
- **Deterministic parser-robustness test** (`tests/fuzz_corpus_replay.rs`).
  - It is a stable-toolchain no-panic gate.
  - It drives `parse_sip`/`parse_sdp`/
    `parse_rtp_header`/`parse_rtcp`.
  - It uses an adversarial seed set and a fixed mutation sweep.
  - It complements the nightly `cargo fuzz` targets.

### Fixed
- **IP-fragmented SIP is now reassembled and decoded** (SNB-0011).
  - After IP fragment reassembly, the buffer is the full IP payload (transport
    header + data).
  - The transport header was never re-parsed.
  - So ports stayed `0`.
  - The SIP parser saw the UDP header before the start line.
  - That dropped the message entirely.
    - An example is a >MTU INVITE with a large SDP on a real NIC.
  - Added `parse::reparse_transport`.
    - It recovers the ports/transport.
    - It strips the header before SIP parsing.
- **Out-of-order TCP: a gap-filling segment now completes a stalled push**
  (SNB-0012).
  - Sometimes the final segment (carrying PSH) arrived before an earlier one.
  - The push could not drain, because of the gap.
  - The later gap-filling segment had no PSH.
  - So the now-contiguous data was buffered forever, and never decoded.
  - The reassembler now remembers a pending push.
  - It flushes once the gap fills.
- **stdio MCP server exits on client disconnect** (SNB-0013).
  - `--mcp` over stdio spun until SIGINT, and ignored stdin EOF.
  - That leaked the process after a client disconnected.
  - The wait loop now also breaks when the stdio serve thread finishes.
  - The HTTP transport only ends on a signal, and this does not affect it.

## [0.4.8] - 2026-06-23

### Fixed
- **TCP: every SIP message in a coalesced segment is now decoded** (SNB-0008).
  - Over TCP, `Content-Length` delimits message boundaries, not packet
    boundaries.
  - So one segment can carry several complete messages.
  - The reassembly consumer previously wrapped each flush as a single message.
  - It parsed only the first, and silently dropped the rest.
  - That is the classic the terminal viewer (#466) weakness.
  - The TCP branch of `PacketProcessor::process` now frames the reassembled
    stream message-by-message (`frame_tcp_sip`):
    - scan to `\r\n\r\n`/`\n\n`,
    - read `Content-Length`, including compact `l`,
    - `message_end = headers_end + CL`.
  - It emits one packet per complete message.
  - A trailing incomplete message is held as bounded per-stream leftover
    (`tcp_sip_leftover`).
  - It is prepended to the next flush.
  - So a body split across segments completes cleanly, instead of being
    false-flagged malformed.
  - On FIN/RST, the held partial is surfaced (truncated) rather than dropped.
  - `sip::is_sip_message` gates the framing.
  - So TLS/WebSocket/binary TCP still passes through whole.

## [0.4.7] - 2026-06-22

### Fixed
- **Dynamic RTP payload types now resolve codec and clock rate from the SDP
  `a=rtpmap`** (SNB-0007).
  - Some streams are created after their SDP.
    - That is the normal order.
    - It is always so in offline pcap replay, where the INVITE/200 is parsed
      before any RTP packet.
  - Those streams were left at the 8 kHz default.
  - They reported `Codec ?`.
  - They reported a wrongly ~11×-inflated RFC-3550 jitter for 90 kHz media.
  - sipnab now remembers the negotiated endpoint, and applies it at stream
    creation.
  - So, for example, H.264 on PT 96 reports `H264 / 90000` with correct
    jitter.
  - The stream associates to its dialog.

### Added
- **TUI call flow: combined transaction/dialog detail.**
  - `a` opens a single scrollable view.
  - It stacks the full raw text of every message in the selected message's
    transaction.
  - `A` does the same for the whole dialog.
- **TUI call flow: transaction filter.**
  - `f` toggles the ladder between two views:
    - only the selected message's transaction (CSeq number + method, with ACK
      folded into its INVITE),
    - and the whole dialog.
- **TUI Name popup: multi-endpoint.**
  - `N` now offers every participant of the flow (or both ends of a
    stream/dialog).
  - `Tab`/`Shift-Tab` switch between them.
  - `Enter` applies all.
  - Previously only the first endpoint was editable.

### Changed
- **TUI call flow: the current row is shown by a full-row highlight**

## [0.4.5] - 2026-06-22

### Added

  - It shows the terminating SIP response behind each dialog's `State`.
    - Examples: `Completed 200`, `Failed 486`, `Canceled 487`.

## [0.4.3] - 2026-06-18

### Added
- Address name resolution (Wireshark-style).
  - It displays `host:port` / `fqdn:port` instead of `ip:port` in:
    - the call list,
    - call-flow participants,
    - and RTP stream views.
  - Press `n` to cycle Off / Static / DNS.
  - Press `N` to name the selected address in context.
    - It is saved to `~/.config/sipnab/hosts`.
  - Sources, in priority order:
    - operator mappings,
    - `/etc/hosts`,
    - then reverse DNS (PTR, on a background worker, off by default).
  - New `--resolve`, `--reverse-dns`, and `--names <FILE>` flags.
  - A new `[names]` config section.
- `--version` / `-V` now embeds the git commit (and a `-dirty` marker),
  alongside the version and feature list.
  - In the TUI, press `v` to show it in the status line.
  - It also appears on the help screen.
- `--setup-caps`: grants the binary the Linux capabilities needed for live
  capture, then exits.
  - It uses `cap_net_raw,cap_net_admin+ep` via `setcap`.
  - So the binary runs without `sudo`.
  - It re-invokes through `sudo` when not already root.
  - An `install.sh` wrapper runs `cargo install`, followed by this step.
- Call flow split view:
  - `Tab` switches keyboard focus between the ladder and detail panes.
    - The focused pane is highlighted, and shown in the status line.
  - Vertical scrollbars appear on either pane when its content overflows.
- The file-open browser (`O`) now lists gzip-compressed captures
  (`*.pcap.gz`, `*.pcapng.gz` and `*.cap.gz`).
  - That matches the loader, which decompresses them.
- pcapng metadata:
  - Name mappings are persisted into a Name Resolution Block (NRB), when
    saving with resolution active.
  - Embedded NRB names are read back when a pcapng is opened.
  - Embedded TLS Decryption Secrets Blocks (DSB) are fed to the decryptor on
    open.
    - A status-line alert says the file carries secrets.
  - `--strip-secrets <OUTPUT>` writes a secret-free copy of an input pcapng,
    without touching the original.
    - It is the `editcap --discard-all-secrets` analog.
  - See `docs/design/pcapng-metadata.md`.

### Security
- SRTP auth-tag verification now uses a constant-time comparison, instead of
  `==`.
  - The API/MCP token check shares it.

  - That closes a MAC timing side channel.
- SRTP session-key derivation now uses the real
  [RFC 3711 section 4.3.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3711.html#section-4.3.1) AES-CM KDF, instead of an HMAC stand-in.
  - The RFC 3711 Appendix B.3 test vectors validate it.
  - So the auth-tag verifier interoperates with standard SRTP.
  - Verification also tries the first two ROC epochs (~131072 packets),
    rather than assuming ROC 0.
  - Long sessions still need stateful ROC tracking.
- SRTP key material is no longer exposed.
  - `SrtpKeyMaterial` has a hand-written `Debug` that redacts the master
    key/salt.
  - The keys are now always wiped on drop.
    - The zeroizing `Drop` was previously gated behind the `tls` feature.
    - So non-tls builds left keys in freed heap.
- SRTP key-parsing error messages no longer echo the candidate base64 key/salt
  bytes.
  - That covers SDP `a=crypto` and the manual key file.
  - They report only the length.
- New `SrtpRocTracker` verifies SRTP auth tags with stateful per-SSRC rollover
  tracking ([RFC 3711 section 3.3.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3711.html#section-3.3.1) index estimation).
  - So streams longer than 65536 packets verify correctly.
  - They no longer rely on the stateless two-epoch guess.
- User resolution (`--user` / privilege drop) now uses the reentrant
  `getpwnam_r`, instead of `getpwnam`.
  - The older call returns a pointer
 into a shared static buffer.
  - A concurrent lookup on another thread can overwrite it mid-read.
  - That data race surfaced as a flaky `nobody`-resolution test.
- TLS 1.2 CBC records are no longer decrypted.
  - Those suites are MAC-then-encrypt.
  - The record MAC was not verified.
  - So a crafted capture could inject forged "decrypted" SIP.
  - The decryptor now declines CBC, and emits nothing.
  - It no longer surfaces unauthenticated plaintext.
  - This does not affect AEAD suites (AES-GCM).
    - `ring` authenticates them on decrypt.
    - They remain the supported path.
- Manual name mappings are now persisted atomically.
  - It writes a temp file in the same directory, then renames it.
  - So an interrupted or failing write can no longer truncate the operator's
    names file.
  - A symlink at the destination is replaced, rather than written through.
- The REST API now refuses to start on a non-loopback bind when no
  authentication is configured.
  - That matches the MCP HTTP transport.
  - It no longer serves an open, unauthenticated read API.
  - Bind `127.0.0.1`, or configure `--api-key` / `--api-signing-key`.
- Manual names are validated (`is_valid_name`) before they reach the
  hosts-format file.
  - So a name containing a newline / tab / control char can no longer inject a
    second host record on round-trip.
  - The in-TUI `N` dialog rejects such names.
  - The serializer skips them, as defense in depth.
- The API and MCP HTTP servers now cap request body size.
- The REST API applies a per-request timeout.
  - So a slow or oversized client cannot pin a connection slot.
- pcapng metadata reading and `--strip-secrets` now reject files above a 2 GiB
  in-memory cap.
  - They no longer risk an OOM on a hostile multi-GB "pcapng".

### Fixed
- Timestamp conversion no longer overflows on a crafted capture/HEP packet.
  - A `tv_usec`/`TS_USEC` outside `[0, 1_000_000)` is clamped before the
    µs→ns multiply.
  - That multiply previously panicked in debug/test builds
    (overflow-checked).
  - It wrapped silently in release.
- File-open browser: when a directory can't be read, it now shows the reason
  and a "run without sudo" hint.
  - It used to show an empty list.
  - The most common cause: sipnab was started with `sudo` and dropped
    privileges to an unprivileged user.
  - That user can't read a `0700` home directory.
- The embedded git commit now refreshes reliably on new commits.
  - The build script watches the resolved `HEAD` ref and `packed-refs`.
- The `-dirty` marker reflects only tracked changes.
  - Untracked scratch paths no longer mark a build dirty.
  - Examples: a local `harness/`, or generated `website/public/`.

## [0.4.1] - 2026-06-12

Not released.

- There is no `v0.4.1` tag and no GitHub release for this version.
- These changes first shipped in 0.4.2.

(Version 0.4.0 was skipped.

- Its tag name was consumed, and then invalidated by an immutable-release
  deletion during the release process.
- No 0.4.0 artifacts were ever published.)

Hardening, performance, and maintainability pass.

- A four-dimension project analysis drove it: maintainability,
  survivability, performance, usability.
- The roadmap and per-item status are in `TODO.md`.

### Added
- Feature-combination CI matrix.
  - Each reduced feature set is compiled with its tests:
    - `native`,
    - `tls`,
    - `api`,
    - `mcp`,
    - `hep`,
    - combinations,
    - and `wasm` lib-only.
  - The documented headless recipe runs the full suite.
  - Fixed the cfg-gating rot this exposed.
    - 7 of 8 reduced combos no longer built their test code.
- HEP listener idle-stall detection.
  - A dead UDP sender produces no error.
  - So sipnab logs one rate-limited warning when no packets arrive for 30 s.
  - It logs one recovery line when traffic resumes.
- `DialogStore::compact_idle`: dialogs idle >10 min keep only their last 20
  messages.
  - That bounds long-run memory.
  - It is wired into the periodic sweeps, with a lifetime eviction counter.
- `PcapWriter::finish()`: flushes buffered output at end of capture, and
  reports the error.
  - Previously a deferred ENOSPC was discarded in `Drop`.
  - That silently truncated the output file, with exit code 0.
- Scanner-kill worker health reporting.
  - A dead worker thread now logs a one-time error.
  - It latches `defense_disabled()`.
  - It no longer silently drops every kill request.
- Invalid pcap timestamps are counted (`INVALID_PCAP_TIMESTAMPS`) and warned
  about.
  - They are no longer silently replaced with the wall clock.
  - A corrupt `tv_usec` no longer overflows in debug builds.
- Structured `sipnab::Error` (thiserror) across the library surface,
  replacing `Result<_, String>`. It covers:
  - config loading/validation,
  - CIDR,
  - alert rules,
  - bind addresses,
  - and CLI validation.
- `sipnab::pipeline`: the per-packet protocol-routing core.
  - It is extracted from `main.rs` as a testable library API.
- Store-layer criterion benchmarks (`store_bench`), and a full-decap
  benchmark.
  - So per-packet costs are measured rather than asserted.
- Filter-DSL parse errors now render:
  - the expression, with a caret at the failing position,
  - a quoting hint for the classic `method == INVITE` mistake,
  - the operator list,
  - and a docs pointer.
- Docs:
  - `docs/examples.md` cookbook (19 recipes),
  - `docs/output-formats.md` (NDJSON schema + jq recipes),
  - `docs/mcp-setup.md` (token bootstrap, systemd unit, troubleshooting),
  - `contrib/sipnabrc.example` (validated by a test against the real config
    loader),
  - and `docs/internals/zero-copy-payloads.md` (design + honest
    measurements).
- Doc-wide drift guard.
  - A test extracts every `--flag` mentioned across all ten user-facing
    markdown files.
  - It asserts each exists in the CLI.
  - README no longer advertises the five filter-DSL aliases as standalone
    flags.
- Build-time warning when the default `audio` feature is enabled for a Linux
  target.
  - It names the libasound2 runtime dependency and the headless build recipe.
- "F1 Help" advertised in the call-list f-key bar at every terminal width.
  - The help overlay was undiscoverable once calls appeared.
- Rustdoc on every public item, enforced with `#![warn(missing_docs)]`.

### Changed
- Zero-copy packet payloads.
  - `Packet.data` and `ParsedPacket.payload` are refcounted `bytes::Bytes`.
  - Payloads are slice views of the captured frame.
  - `SipMessage.raw`/`.body` share the same buffer via `parse_sip_bytes`.
  - `SipMessage::clone` (dialog-store insertion) no longer copies message
    bytes.
  - Measured honestly: cost-neutral at typical packet sizes.
    - The copies it removes were already ~15 ns.
  - Shipped for:
    - large-payload behavior,
    - allocator pressure,
    - and the structural simplification.
  - See `docs/internals/zero-copy-payloads.md`.
- `src/tui/mod.rs` (5,278 lines) split into `theme.rs`, `render.rs`,
  `events.rs`, `save.rs`.
  - State/App/entry point remain.
  - Pure code motion.
  - All TUI state tests and snapshots unchanged.
- Synthetic-packet construction moved from the TUI to `output::synthetic`.
  - That removes a TUI→capture layering violation.
- Dialog-store and reassembler eviction is batched (max(1, cap/100) per O(n)
  pass).
  - Consider a unique-Call-ID or fragment flood at capacity.
  - Per-insert cost drops ~50x.
  - The per-fragment warn! log flood becomes one summary line per batch.
  - Stores may sit up to one batch below the cap.
  - The cap remains a hard upper bound.
- Audio payload buffering is disabled in batch mode.
  - Nothing there can read it.
  - TUI on-demand WAV export/playback is unchanged.
- Test suites no longer use fixed sleeps.
  - Deadline polling replaces the 13 timing-dependent waits in the security
    and process-isolation tests.

### Fixed
- Retransmission detection is O(1), via a per-dialog seen-CSeq set.
  - ~25x faster per in-dialog message.
  - It survives message compaction.
  - The previous stored-message scan re-parsed every CSeq header.
  - It forgot history once messages were capped or compacted.
- RTCP report matching is O(1), via an SSRC index (~10x at 1000 streams).
  - It preserves first-match insertion-order semantics across eviction.
- Dialog lookup no longer allocates a Call-ID `String` per message.
- `--filter`/`--json`/`--no-cli-print` help text documents:
  - alias acceptance,
  - NDJSON,
  - and summary-only usage.

### Analysis notes
- Several externally-reported findings were verified as invalid.
- `TODO.md` records them with evidence:
  - the multiple-stream-store-locks claim,
  - HEP cumulative-memory exhaustion,
  - the unwrap-density audit (all flagged unwraps are in test code),
  - and the projected 20-30% hot-path win from payload copies (refuted by A/B
    measurement).

## [0.3.2] - 2026-05-05

### Added
- `--filter` now accepts diagnostic alias names directly:
  - `codec-asym`,
  - `ptime-asym`,
  - `payload-asym`,
  - `duration-asym`,
  - `late-media`,
  - plus the five existing `--problems`/`--slow-setup`/`--short-calls`/
    `--one-way`/
    `--nat-issues` aliases.
  - Raw DSL expressions still parse as before.
  - Alias resolution is tried first, and falls back to the parser.
- `--no-cli-print` flag: suppress per-message CLI output.
  - So only the post-capture summary (`--report` / `--call-report`) reaches
    stdout.
- `--version` now lists the Cargo features compiled into the binary.
  - Example:
    `sipnab 0.3.2 (abc12345) features: native,tui,audio,tls,hep,api,mcp,mcp-http`.
  - That makes it trivial to confirm a server build was produced with the
    expected feature set.
    - For example, that `mcp-http` is present.

### Changed
- Documentation refreshed for the three flag changes above:
  - filter-DSL reference,
  - CLI reference,
  - install verification,
  - cookbook recipes "Find why a call sounds bad in one direction only" and
    "Generate a call report (text / Markdown / JSON)".

- **MCP server mode (Phase 8).**
  - Run sipnab as a Model Context Protocol server.
  - So an AI agent, such as Claude Code or Claude Desktop, can drive read-only
    analysis.
  - Two transports:
    - `--mcp` (stdio, requires `mcp` feature) for local agents.
    - `--mcp --mcp-transport http` (requires `mcp-http` feature) for remote
      agents.
      - Bearer-token auth via `--mcp-token` / `--mcp-token-file` /
        `SIPNAB_MCP_TOKEN`.
      - Non-loopback binds without a token are refused at startup.
- `--mcp-bind`, `--mcp-token`, `--mcp-token-file`, `--mcp-allowed-host` CLI
  flags for the HTTP transport.
  - `--mcp-allowed-host <HOST>` extends rmcp's DNS-rebind allowlist.
    - The default is `localhost`/`127.0.0.1`/`::1`.
  - So clients connecting via the public hostname or IP aren't rejected.
- Eleven read-only MCP tools:
  - `list_dialogs`,
  - `get_dialog_report`,
  - `find_problems`,
  - `get_dialog`,
  - `get_message`,
  - `render_ladder`,
  - `rtp_stats`,
  - `search_messages`,
  - `tail_dialogs`,
  - `security_findings`,
  - `stats`.
  - `HARD_LIMIT = 1000` per call bounds all of them.
- A new in-memory `FindingsHistory` ring buffer backs `security_findings`.
  - The default is 1000 entries.
  - So recent scanner / fraud / digest-leak / reg-flood alerts can be queried
    after the fact.
- Five per-call asymmetry diagnostic signals (Phase 8.7), with matching
  filter-DSL fields and aliases:
  - `codec_asymmetry` / `codec-asym`
    - A/B legs negotiated different codecs.
  - `ptime_asymmetry` / `ptime-asym`
    - Different packetization intervals.
  - `payload_asymmetry` / `payload-asym`
    - Dynamic PT mismatch with matching codec.
  - `duration_asymmetry` / `duration-asym`
    - Materially shorter media on one leg.
  - `late_media` / `late-media`
    - RTP starts noticeably after the answering 200 OK.
- Interactive file-open browser for loading pcaps:
  - directory listing with pcap filter,
  - typed narrowing,
  - manual-path mode,
  - and selection state.
- `contrib/observability/`
  - A Docker Compose stack: Prometheus + OTel Collector + Tempo + Grafana.
  - Plus a sample `sipnab-hep.service` systemd unit.
  - It runs identically on a Mac dev box and on a dedicated capture host.
  - Switch via `SIPNAB_HOST` in `.env`.
- `scripts/deploy-website.sh`
  - An environment-agnostic Zola build + rsync helper for static-hosting
    deploys (`DEPLOY_HOST` env var).

### Changed
- Logging facade migrated to `tracing` (Phase 8.0b).
  - `tracing` is now unconditional.
  - `tracing-subscriber` is gated under `native`.
  - The `--mcp` stdio path requires `--quiet` (or no other stdout-writing
    flags).
    - So log lines on stdout do not clobber JSON-RPC.
- End-of-capture summary now distinguishes RTP packets from RTP streams.
  - It reports `N RTP packets across M streams`, instead of conflating the
    two.
- "No SIP traffic found" guidance softened to a media-only notice when RTP was
  successfully parsed.
  - So media-only pcaps no longer look like parse failures.
- Documentation refresh on www.sipnab.com:
  - new MCP page,
  - new Enabling MCP / Runtime Dependencies / Cross-glibc sections in the
    install guide,
  - full feature-flag table now matches `Cargo.toml`,
  - homepage feature row for MCP,
  - REST-API ↔ MCP cross-reference.

### Fixed
- **`--hep-listen` was silently dropping every received packet.**
  - The listener built a `Packet` with `link_type = DLT_RAW`, plus
    payload-only data (no IP/UDP headers).
  - The parser then mis-read SIP body bytes as IP headers.
  - `processor.process()` swallowed the resulting parse errors.
  - The fix has two parts:
    - `PreParsed` metadata on `Packet` (src/dst addr+port, IP protocol),
    - and a short-circuit in `parse_packet` that uses the metadata directly
      when present.
  - The HEP listener now passes addressing through unchanged.
  - Verified end-to-end with synthetic HEP injection.
  - Dialogs and metrics now populate.
- `cargo build --no-default-features` no longer fails with 32 errors.
  - The `privilege`, `process_isolation`, and `signals` modules were gated
    only on `not(target_arch = "wasm32")`.
  - But each pulls a dependency (`libc`, `crossbeam-channel`) that's only
    present under the `native` feature.
  - The fixes:
    - added `feature = "native"` to those gates,
    - set `required-features = ["native"]` on both `[[bin]]` entries,
    - made `hep = ["native"]` (was `[]`),
    - and added `serde` to `chrono`'s feature list, so `--features api`
      compiles.
  - These now all build standalone with `--no-default-features`:
    - `--features hep`,
    - `--features audio`,
    - `--features mcp`,
    - `--features mcp-http`,
    - `--features tls`,
    - and `--features api`.
- Audio playback init no longer corrupts the TUI on hosts without a usable
  audio device.
  - Examples: Tegra/Jetson Ubuntu, headless.
  - libasound stderr is redirected to `/dev/null` during device open.
  - A failed init is cached.
  - So repeated `P` presses don't retry and re-spam the terminal.
- Failed audio init now surfaces an actionable message.
  - It suggests `F2 Save WAV` as an offline alternative.
- The bundled `contrib/observability/` Grafana dashboard and Prometheus alert
  rules now reference correct metric names:
  - `sipnab_mos_bucket` (was `sipnab_rtp_mos_bucket`),
  - `sum(sipnab_dialogs_total{state=~
    "trying|ringing|incall"})` for the active-dialog gauge.
    - It was `sipnab_active_dialogs`, which doesn't exist.
- Compiler/clippy warnings:
  - silenced `function_casts_as_integer` in signal handlers,
  - resolved all warnings in tests.

- Zero-copy SIP parser with compact header support and header folding
